newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CanWest says Australia/N.Z. profits rise.
newsitem.headline: CanWest says Australia/N.Z. profits rise.

text.p: Canadian television broadcaster CanWest Global Communications Corp said its Australian and New Zealand operations achieved higher sales and operating profits in the nine months to May 31.

The company said the Australian operations of Network Ten contributed a 39.5 percent rise in group revenue to C$268.65 million, reflecting the addition of stations in Perth and Adelaide which were acquired in late 1995 as well as foreign exchange gains. Revenue rose by 8.3 percent on a same-station basis.
CanWest, which owns a disputed 76 percent stake in Ten, said the network's contribution to group operating profit rose 35.3 percent to C$92.93 million in the nine months.
The company's share of Ten's third quarter revenue rose by 41.6 percent rise to C$97.47 million and its contribution to group operating profit rose by 35.5 percent to C$32.97 million.

The TV3 operations in New Zealand contributed C$69.29 million to group revenue in the latest nine months, a rise of 117 percent. CanWest said this reflected full consolidation of TV3's results from November last year and the inclusion of the company's share of an additional two months in the first
CanWest said that TV3's revenues on a comparable basis were four percent higher in the nine months, reflecting audience share gains and a higher share of revenue in a soft advertising market.
TV3's operating profit contribution to CanWest rose by 99.3 percent to C$21.52 million and on a same-period basis was comparable with the previous year.
CanWest said TV3's third quarter revenue contribution rose by 156.9 percent to C$23.59 million and its profit contribution rose to C$5.06 million from C$1.29 million a year ago.
